chapters.title: Start here
chapters.intro: Choose your role, search for a job you need to do, and follow the short steps. This guide covers the current application; your permissions decide which controls appear.

steps.title: Choose your view
steps.text: Use the role selector to narrow the guide. Agent is for daily staff work; Admin includes setup and access; Customer is for the support portal.

steps.title: Find a task
steps.text: Type a word such as attachment, timer, Outlook or import in Search this manual. Select a chapter from the results.

steps.title: Follow and check
steps.text: Tick a step after reading it. These ticks are saved in this browser only. They do not complete a real task or change Worktello.

steps.title: Inspect a screenshot
steps.text: Select an image to enlarge it. Read its evidence caption: production, isolated synthetic QA and an untested action are different things.

steps.title: Keep a local copy
steps.text: Keep this manual folder together. For a portable copy with linked technical records, use the generated ZIP and extract its complete folder tree. Live app links require internet and your own account.

notes: Updated 25 October 2026. Technical COEX identifiers and the coex.digisol.ae hostname remain compatible with the Worktello name.
This is a complete module reference, not a claim that every workflow was freshly tested on every device. Chapters state their evidence limits.

chapters.title: Sign in and recover access
chapters.intro: Use the account provided by your organization. Staff and customers use different views on the same sign-in page.

steps.title: Open sign-in
steps.text: Open the production sign-in page. Select Agent for staff access or Customer for the support portal.

steps.title: Choose a method
steps.text: Staff can use Continue with Microsoft when their Microsoft identity is linked. Otherwise use the email and password supplied by your administrator.

steps.title: Remember carefully
steps.text: Remember me on this PC keeps a password session for up to 60 days. Choose it only on a trusted personal computer.

steps.title: Recover a password
steps.text: Use Forgot your password and follow the reset message. Never share a password, reset link, verification code or session token in a ticket.

steps.title: Sign out
steps.text: Use your avatar menu and Sign out on a shared device. Administrators may expire old sessions during a release; sign in again when asked.

notes: A Microsoft account alone does not create Worktello access. The account must match an active staff identity.
Browser Microsoft sign-in to production was verified on 25 October. Customer portal interaction evidence comes from isolated synthetic QA.
images: staff-sign-in.png
Actual production staff sign-in • blank credentials • 25 October 2026

chapters.title: Profile, theme and notifications
chapters.intro: Use the avatar/account menu for your personal settings. Available options vary between staff and customer accounts.

steps.title: Open your account menu
steps.text: Select your avatar at the top right. Review Edit profile, What’s new, notification and sign-out options that are available.

steps.title: Edit your profile
steps.text: Update your own name/job title in the provided profile form. Account identity/access changes may need an administrator.

steps.title: Choose your theme
steps.text: Use the theme control for the supported Light/Dark/Sunset choices.

steps.title: Enable notifications intentionally
steps.text: Use Browser notifications if you want them. Browser alerts work while the application is open in another tab; closed-browser push is not claimed.

steps.title: Review updates
steps.text: What’s new summarizes user-facing changes. Its acknowledgement applies to the current release, not every future update.

chapters.title: Your daily workspace
chapters.intro: Dashboard is an overview. My Desk is the work you choose to focus on today. The Tasks list can include shared work that remains open for others.

steps.title: Review your work
steps.text: Open Dashboard to review assigned work, due dates and visible team indicators. A badge is a scoped count; it does not replace the filters on a list.

steps.title: Choose today’s focus
steps.text: Use Add to My Desk on a task you intend to work on. Open My Desk to focus on those selections.

steps.title: Finish your commitment
steps.text: Use the available completion action when your work is finished. The office day closes automatically using the configured office timezone.

steps.title: Use the right completion
steps.text: My subtask done clears your personal active view of a shared task. It does not close the main task for everyone.

notes: A shared task can stay open while other assignees continue. Do not close the whole task simply to clear your own list.

chapters.title: Find work quickly
chapters.intro: Use the search in the application header, or Cmd+K on Mac / Ctrl+K on Windows.

steps.title: Open search
steps.text: Select Search tasks, spaces, customers in the header. The popup opens beside the visible search control.

steps.title: Enter at least two letters
steps.text: Search by a useful title, customer/Space name or task number. Wait for Searching to finish before choosing a result.

steps.title: Open a result
steps.text: Use the pointer or keyboard to choose a visible result. Your existing access permissions still apply.

steps.title: Close without leaving
steps.text: Press Escape or Close search. You return to the screen you were working on.

notes: The popup was corrected to render above the page header. Earlier local QA covered 390, 700, 768 and desktop widths; physical touch/keyboard testing remains separate.
Production search returned an existing permitted task on 25 October.

chapters.title: Create, find and update a task
chapters.intro: A task belongs to Personal or an accessible Space. A Folder can organize work inside a Space.

steps.title: Narrow the list
steps.text: Open Tasks and use the available owner, Space and personal-work filters. Search by title or task number when you already know the item.

steps.title: Create in the right place
steps.text: Choose Add task or the quick-create control. Select Personal or a Space, then the available Folder. Check the destination before writing private information.

steps.title: Set responsibility
steps.text: Enter a clear title and description. Choose assignees, priority, dates and an estimate when needed. Available people and actions follow your permissions.

steps.title: Review before saving
steps.text: Check who will receive the assignment and whether the Space/Folder is appropriate. Save once; do not create another task just because an email is delayed.

steps.title: Use preview or full page
steps.text: Select the task title to open its quick drawer, or use the full-page control for the complete conversation, attachments and history.

steps.title: Change status carefully
steps.text: Use the permitted status action when work moves forward. Closing the main task affects all assignees; use personal completion for just your subtask work.

notes: Task creation may queue an assignment email for another person according to tenant email settings. Self-assignment mail remains intentionally suppressed.
This guide does not create production tasks as examples.
images: outlook-create.png
Task form inside production Outlook • same staff task concepts • blank and not submitted • 25 October 2026

chapters.title: Finish your subtask, keep shared work open
chapters.intro: My subtask done is a personal focus control. The task can remain open for colleagues.

steps.title: Complete the real subtask
steps.text: Open the task and mark your assigned subtask complete when its work is finished. Check the updated completion count.

steps.title: Clear your active view
steps.text: Choose My subtask done when you want the shared task removed from your active work/My Desk view.

steps.title: Find it later
steps.text: Use Mine → My subtask done or All my work, where available, to find personally completed shared work.

steps.title: Resume if needed
steps.text: Choose Resume my work when you want it active again. New or reopened assigned subtasks can bring the task back automatically.

notes: Personal completion does not close the main task, complete another person’s subtask, or remove their access.
The controlled checkbox/count fix was verified with a synthetic record, reload and reversal; ordinary-account production mutations were not repeated.

chapters.title: Spaces, Folders and board views
chapters.intro: Use Spaces for shared work and Folders for organization. Personal work has its own visibility rules.

steps.title: Open the right Space
steps.text: Select Spaces and open an accessible Space. Use a Folder when the Space is divided into work areas.

steps.title: Choose a view
steps.text: Use the board/list/timeline controls available on that Space. Filters narrow the visible records without moving or deleting them.

steps.title: Move work deliberately
steps.text: A status move changes the task’s workflow. Review the task and intended stage before dragging or saving a status change.

steps.title: Review completed work
steps.text: Done tasks can remain in the board’s Done column. Use the available visibility control to hide them if you need a clearer active view.

steps.title: Archive with care
steps.text: Administrators can archive a Space or Folder through settings. Read whether its tasks are archived too or retained in the Space; restore through the corresponding archived view.

notes: Being an assignee does not bypass a private Space or Folder boundary.
Archiving and hiding are different operations. Do not archive shared work merely to clear your own list.

chapters.title: Plan dates on the timeline
chapters.intro: The Space timeline uses Dubai office time. Preview date changes first; save only when the intended schedule is clear.

steps.title: Find the right scale
steps.text: Use Fit, Today, Week, Month or Quarter. Adjust zoom and the task-name column when the chart is crowded.

steps.title: Select one task
steps.text: Choose the task’s date control or bar. Closed tasks do not expose schedule editing; unscheduled tasks remain visible in their section.

steps.title: Preview a move or resize
steps.text: Move a bar to change its schedule, or resize an edge. Choose day, hour or half-hour snapping; keyboard equivalents are available.

steps.title: Check the exact dates
steps.text: Read the date preview in office time. An end before a start is invalid. Only one date preview is edited at a time.

steps.title: Save or discard
steps.text: Save writes the dates. Discard restores the displayed stored dates without a save. Reloading an unsaved preview keeps the original stored schedule.

steps.title: Undo a recent save
steps.text: Undo last save reverses the last save in this mounted chart, provided nobody has changed those dates. Undo does not survive a reload.

notes: A stale/concurrent edit is rejected rather than silently overwriting someone else’s dates. Reload and review the current schedule before trying again.
Images below are actual application captures from isolated Docker QA with synthetic records, not production customer work. Physical touch and two-browser collision UI testing were not performed.

chapters.title: Conversations, updates and mentions
chapters.intro: Keep progress with the task so colleagues can follow its history.

steps.title: Open the conversation
steps.text: Use the full task page or quick drawer. The main reply/update box sits above the conversation.

steps.title: Choose the order
steps.text: Use Ascending or Descending where available. The drawer shows latest updates first; Show more reveals older threads.

steps.title: Write a useful update
steps.text: State what changed, any blocker and the next step. Use a mention only when that colleague needs to act or know.

steps.title: Attach evidence
steps.text: Paste, drop or choose supported files. Check the thumbnail/filename before posting; remove the wrong selection first.

steps.title: Post once and verify
steps.text: Review the saved thread before retrying. You can edit your own update where the control is available; edited notes are labelled.

notes: Task updates linked to a support ticket stay internal and are not customer replies. To communicate with a customer, use the ticket’s public reply control.
A mention may trigger an email under existing rules. Do not send a test mention to a real colleague for a demonstration.

chapters.title: Documents, images and attachments
chapters.intro: Use the attachment picker with an update/reply. A preview lets you check what will be posted.

steps.title: Select the destination first
steps.text: Open the correct task, ticket or portal conversation before choosing files.

steps.title: Add files
steps.text: Paste an image, drop supported files, or use the attach/upload option provided beside the update or reply.

steps.title: Check the preview
steps.text: Confirm image thumbnails and filenames. Remove accidental selections before posting. An image-only update is supported where implemented.

steps.title: Find existing files
steps.text: On the full task page, open Documents & attachments on the right. It collects accessible task attachments so you do not need to scroll through every update.

steps.title: Open or download safely
steps.text: Use the saved thumbnail/filename to preview or download. Permissions are checked; an inaccessible attachment is not made public by its URL.

notes: Image limit: 3 MB per image; message total: 10 MB. The customer portal also caps attachments at 10 files. Read any additional file-specific message shown by the picker.
The task quick drawer does not have a separate Documents tab. Production clipboard-to-post acceptance remains a separate check; no private files are uploaded by this manual.

chapters.title: Timers and manual time
chapters.intro: Log the work you actually do. Your own time and other people’s totals are separate views.

steps.title: Start on the right item
steps.text: Open the task or ticket and use its timer control. Starting a timer follows the application’s rule for stopping your previous running timer.

steps.title: Stop when finished
steps.text: Stop the timer at the end of the work. Review the saved entry in your timesheet.

steps.title: Add missed time manually
steps.text: Use Add time when you forgot the timer. Choose the correct date and duration, add a clear note and set Billable only when appropriate.

steps.title: Correct transparently
steps.text: Use the edit/remove action available to you and provide a reason. Locked weeks and running-entry rules still apply.

steps.title: Review the week
steps.text: Open My timesheet and check dates, notes and totals. Use permitted team reports for wider visibility; normal agents do not gain access to everyone’s time.

notes: Do not start a production timer merely to see the control: it can stop your existing timer.
App task times use Dubai office time. Read the displayed date/time before saving, especially when travelling.

chapters.title: Handle support tickets
chapters.intro: Use a public reply for customer communication and an internal note for staff-only discussion.

steps.title: Find the ticket
steps.text: Open Support → Tickets. Filter by the available queue, assignment and status controls. Select the subject for preview or full detail.

steps.title: Check customer and sending identity
steps.text: Review the linked customer/contact, CC list and configured Reply to customer sender before sending.

steps.title: Read in the order you prefer
steps.text: Choose Ascending or Descending message order. Use Show more for older messages and Read more for long text.

steps.title: Choose public or internal
steps.text: Select the intended reply/note type explicitly. Customer messages have purple glow, agent replies green and internal notes red; color is only a visual aid.

steps.title: Attach and review
steps.text: Preview files/images and check the body and recipients. A public reply can send email; internal task notes remain private.

steps.title: Resolve or close correctly
steps.text: Choose a permitted status when support work is complete. A resolved/closed ticket stops its running timer under existing service rules.

notes: The red internal-note style is not a substitute for checking the note/reply mode.
Tutorial link/permission failures and sending failures should be diagnosed before repeatedly resubmitting the same content.

chapters.title: Customers and contacts
chapters.intro: Keep company and contact information with the customer record. Available editing depends on your permissions.

steps.title: Find before adding
steps.text: Open CRM → Customers and search for the company/contact. Avoid creating a second record for the same customer.

steps.title: Review the customer
steps.text: Open its detail to see permitted contacts, history, opportunities and contracts.

steps.title: Maintain contact information
steps.text: Add or update the appropriate contact through the available form. Check the email/mobile before using it in communication.

steps.title: Use portal access deliberately
steps.text: An authorized administrator can create a portal account for an eligible active contact. Share its one-time credentials securely; an invitation email is not automatically sent.

notes: Customer portal access is linked to the contact/company, not granted to anyone who knows an email address.
Existing customer exports contain core fields only, not every contact/document/history field.

chapters.title: Qualify and convert a lead
chapters.intro: A lead records a possible customer before qualification. Conversion connects it to a customer and, optionally, an opportunity.

steps.title: Record the lead
steps.text: Open CRM → Leads and use the permitted add form. Enter useful identity/contact/source and ownership information.

steps.title: Check duplicate warnings
steps.text: Review any match for email, mobile or company. A warning helps you avoid duplicates; do not ignore it without checking.

steps.title: Keep the stage current
steps.text: Mark work in progress or disqualify with a reason where appropriate. Reopen if the circumstances change.

steps.title: Convert when qualified
steps.text: Use Convert, choose a new or existing customer, and review the contact. Optionally create an opportunity and choose its salesperson.

notes: Conversion is a business-record mutation; review the destination and owner before confirming.
The lead remains marked Converted with a customer link and retained history.

chapters.title: Manage the sales pipeline
chapters.intro: An opportunity tracks a potential sale, its owner, stage, value and next action.

steps.title: Create the deal
steps.text: Choose the customer/contact, owner, expected close date, value/currency, products and available quote reference.

steps.title: Set a next step
steps.text: Add a clear next action and date so the deal does not become an unexplained open record.

steps.title: Move through stages
steps.text: Use the list/board controls to move the deal. Read additional requirements when marking Won or Lost.

steps.title: Close accurately
steps.text: Give the required loss reason, or review the optional contract creation after winning. An offered contract remains a draft until activated.

notes: Currencies are kept separate; a total in one currency is not automatically comparable with another.
Stage probabilities and loss reasons are administrator-managed. This chapter is a guide, not a fresh production sales mutation test.

chapters.title: Maintain the product list
chapters.intro: Products describe the things sold or covered by customer agreements.

steps.title: Search for an existing product
steps.text: Open CRM → Products and find the item by its name/code before adding another.

steps.title: Use a consistent code
steps.text: Create or edit through the permitted form. Keep codes consistent when products are referenced in CSV imports or contracts.

steps.title: Review related agreements
steps.text: Check the intended product and pricing information before using it on a customer contract.

notes: CSV transfer covers core product fields; detailed service models/parent configuration are not a complete round trip.

chapters.title: Manage contracts and renewals
chapters.intro: Contracts keep agreement dates, products, billing information and renewal follow-up together.

steps.title: Review the agreement
steps.text: Choose the customer, dates, amount/currency, billing interval, products and document link through the allowed form.

steps.title: Check before activation
steps.text: Review a draft before activating it. A renewal prepares the next term; activation can retire the prior contract.

steps.title: Follow expiry indicators
steps.text: Use Expiring/Expired and renewal filters. Customer warnings use configured thresholds; contract-owner email reminders depend on tenant settings.

steps.title: Record invoicing accurately
steps.text: Use Mark invoiced only after the invoice has actually been raised in the connected business process.

steps.title: Preview messages
steps.text: When using the contract email action, select recipients/template and review the message before sending.

notes: A manual walkthrough does not send a renewal message, activate a contract or mark a real invoice.
Core CSV contract transfer excludes detailed service lines and is not a full contract backup.

chapters.title: Customer support portal
chapters.intro: Customers can raise and follow their own support tickets. Staff and internal notes stay outside the customer view.

steps.title: Use the provided account
steps.text: Select Customer at sign-in and use your support account. There is no public self-signup that claims access by email alone.

steps.title: Find your ticket
steps.text: Use My tickets, search and status filters. Only tickets linked to your permitted contact/company identity are listed.

steps.title: Raise a request
steps.text: Choose Raise ticket, enter a clear subject/message and attach relevant evidence. Review files before submitting.

steps.title: Reply on the conversation
steps.text: Open the ticket and send a public customer reply. Pending/resolved tickets may reopen on reply; closed or merged tickets ask for a new ticket.

steps.title: Maintain your profile
steps.text: Use the account menu for profile, password reset, browser notification opt-in and sign-out.

notes: Customers cannot see internal staff notes, private task discussions, staff timers or another contact’s tickets.
Do not put passwords, verification codes or unnecessary personal/medical documents in a support request. Customer account provisioning and live email delivery are separate administrator checks.
images: customer-sign-in.png
Actual production customer sign-in • blank credentials • portal write flows not repeated • 25 October 2026

chapters.title: Use Worktello inside Microsoft Teams
chapters.intro: The existing organization app opens a personal workspace with your accessible tasks. It uses your linked Microsoft staff identity.

steps.title: Open the organization app
steps.text: In Teams, open Apps and choose Worktello from the organization’s available apps. If it is already pinned, select its rail icon.

steps.title: View your work
steps.text: Use My Tasks, Search tasks and the personal-work filter. With the separate view-others permission, select agents; shared tasks appear once.

steps.title: Read task detail
steps.text: Select a task to read updates, assignment and your time controls. Open full Worktello for attachments/full-page features.

steps.title: Use your time controls
steps.text: Start/stop your timer or add/edit your own time with a reason. These controls always act as the signed-in person, not a selected agent.

steps.title: Create or assign where allowed
steps.text: Use Create task to choose Space, Folder, assignees, dates and time in the form. Assigning other people needs its own permission; it does not grant private destination access.

steps.title: Create from a message
steps.text: Where the message action is available, use More actions → Create Worktello task and review the destination/content before saving.

notes: Real Teams web SSO, list and task-detail rendering were verified. Production timer/time edits, posting, reassignment and creation were not mutated for the demonstration.
Desktop/mobile and ordinary-account device acceptance remain separate. Some capabilities, including task sharing, vary by host.

chapters.title: Use Worktello inside Outlook web
chapters.intro: Outlook can surface the same personal workspace. The server and Microsoft authorization must both permit Outlook web.

steps.title: Open Outlook web
steps.text: Sign in to Outlook with your organization’s Microsoft account.

steps.title: Open the app picker
steps.text: Select the Apps/grid control in the left rail. Choose Worktello from the available app list.

steps.title: Wait for sign-in
steps.text: The embedded workspace should load using the linked staff account. Your normal Worktello permissions apply.

steps.title: Review before using actions
steps.text: Search/open your tasks. Review time and assignment controls before saving; do not start a timer solely as a visual test.

steps.title: If content is refused
steps.text: Capture the visible error and report the host URL. An administrator must check the exact embedding policy and Outlook web authorization; do not disable browser protections.

notes: Production Outlook web SSO, task list and an accessible task detail were verified after the scoped fix. Assignment/time/update controls and the blank create form rendered. No task, time entry, assignment or message was submitted.
Outlook desktop/mobile, creating from an email and Copilot features are not claimed by the Supported on badge or this personal-tab fix.

chapters.title: Share a task link to Teams
chapters.intro: Sharing opens a review/recipient flow. Worktello does not silently send a direct chat message.

steps.title: Choose the task
steps.text: Open the full task page, quick drawer or supported Teams detail.

steps.title: Review the preview
steps.text: Select Share task to Teams and check the number, title, status and authenticated task link.

steps.title: Choose the recipient in Teams
steps.text: Continue to the supported Microsoft sharing interface. Choose the chat/person and review before sending.

steps.title: Use a manual link if needed
steps.text: If native sharing is unavailable, use the provided copy/link fallback. The recipient still needs access to open the task.

notes: The share preview excludes internal descriptions, attachment data, tokens and customer details. A title may itself contain private information: check the audience.
Localhost sharing is disabled. Sharing does not copy chat history, synchronize conversations or automatically reply to a source message.

chapters.title: Setup and organization settings
chapters.intro: Setup opens a tabbed workspace over the current work page. Only permitted tabs and actions appear.

steps.title: Open Setup
steps.text: Select Setup from the rail/sidebar/mobile menu. Queues is the initial tab when permitted; otherwise the first available tab opens.

steps.title: Choose the setting
steps.text: Tabs include Queues, Tutorials, Email, Pipeline, WhatsApp, Saved replies, Tenant settings, Custom fields, Import and export and Tenants according to your rights.

steps.title: Review before applying
steps.text: Read what a setting changes and who it affects. Preview messages/videos where available; confirm real sender identities and destinations.

steps.title: Return to your work
steps.text: Use Close setup or Escape. Direct Setup URLs can be opened again and the return path keeps the originating page/filter context.

notes: Setup visibility is not authorization by itself: the server checks each operation.
WhatsApp and tutorial integrations depend on their actual configuration; a visible tab does not mean every external channel is connected.
images: import-export.png
Actual production Setup → Import and export • no file uploaded or business export downloaded • 25 October 2026

chapters.title: Import and export CSV records
chapters.intro: Use Setup → Import and export. Imports create new records and skip recognized matches; they do not overwrite existing records.

steps.title: Check permissions and order
steps.text: You need administrator/module access. Start with customers and products before linked contracts, tasks and tickets.

steps.title: Choose a record type
steps.text: Select Tasks, Tickets, Customers, Leads, Products or Contracts.

steps.title: Download its template
steps.text: Use Download template and keep its case-sensitive headings. Prepare up to 500 records and 2 MB per import.

steps.title: Preview the exact file
steps.text: Upload and Preview import. Correct every invalid row first. A changed/expired preview requires another preview; approval lasts 15 minutes.

steps.title: Review and import
steps.text: Read the ready/skipped/invalid results. Confirm only the intended creates. Existing numbering, assignment and alert rules still apply.

steps.title: Review the outcome
steps.text: Check created/skipped/failed results. A runtime failure can leave a partial import; retry skips recognized matches already created.

steps.title: Export core records
steps.text: Use Export CSV for accessible core records, up to 10,000. Treat downloaded business data as private.

notes: Attachments, conversations, custom fields, contacts and detailed product/contract configuration are excluded. This is not a complete backup/restore or assignment round trip.
Exported _id/_number/_status/_owner/_assignees/_folder metadata is for reference and ignored on import. Private task boundaries remain enforced.

All six modules passed isolated database and synthetic browser QA. A production task template download was verified; no real production import/export of business records was performed for this manual.

chapters.title: Users, roles and access
chapters.intro: Grant only the access a person needs. Viewing, assigning and time ownership are separate rules.

steps.title: Review the account
steps.text: Open Security → Users and roles. Confirm the intended active staff identity and organization before editing.

steps.title: Choose permissions deliberately
steps.text: Use the documented roles/grants/denials. Explicit denials win where the permission system defines them.

steps.title: Separate Teams rights
steps.text: View other agents’ tasks and Assign tasks to others are independent permissions. Neither bypasses private Spaces/Folders.

steps.title: Keep time ownership clear
steps.text: Teams time actions remain for the signed-in agent even when an administrator can view other people’s tasks.

steps.title: Record a change
steps.text: Use a reason/audit process for sensitive access changes and test the intended role with an authorized test account.

notes: The manual never grants permissions or adds Microsoft clients just by being opened. New security-sensitive authorization requires explicit action-time approval.
Secrets, environment files and token values do not belong in a manual, screenshot, commit or support conversation.

chapters.title: Problems, fixes and verification
chapters.intro: Every resolution has a dated record. A green test alone is not proof that production or a native Microsoft client works.

steps.title: Record the symptom
steps.text: Capture the exact safe error text, affected screen, date and a screenshot. Exclude credentials, tokens and confidential record contents.

steps.title: Confirm the cause
steps.text: Separate evidence from a guess. Check the running revision/configuration as well as local source.

steps.title: Apply the smallest fix
steps.text: Keep tenant/user access boundaries, preserve unrelated work and use the required approval for new security-sensitive access.

steps.title: Verify at each layer
steps.text: Record tests, build/CI, actual deployment and a real browser acceptance check separately. Name any device/write flow not exercised.

steps.title: Update this manual
steps.text: Add the dated resolution, link its chapter, store safe screenshots locally and in the repository, and retain old evidence as history.

notes: Resolution cards below describe documented history. The detailed Markdown record is the source for exact commit, deployment and rollback evidence.

chapters.title: Files, local copies and developer handover
chapters.intro: The application, documentation and images remain in the local project folder and are versioned in GitHub. Secrets remain separate.

steps.title: Start from current state
steps.text: Read ai/CURRENT_TASK.md and ai/HANDOFF.md before continuing. Historical notes are retained; a newer verified entry supersedes a pending one.

steps.title: Understand the files
steps.text: .tsx files build interactive React screens. .ts files hold services, validation, permissions and tests. .md files hold readable technical/QA/deployment records.

steps.title: Keep the manual together
steps.text: docs/manual contains the HTML, CSS, JavaScript, assets, manifest and blank downloads. docs/resolutions contains dated diagnosis/fix/verification records.

steps.title: Distinguish local, cloud and live
steps.text: A local file is not automatically committed. A pushed commit is not automatically deployed. Use the actual application SHA/process/health evidence before saying live.

steps.title: Preserve private configuration
steps.text: Do not copy .env files, PEM keys, tokens, private exports or backups into the manual or GitHub. Keep unrelated projects/ and persistent Docker volumes untouched.

steps.title: Prepare rollback
steps.text: Follow deploy/ZERO-DOWNTIME.md, current active slots and exact release notes. Never assume the original server checkout is the active web or worker directory.

notes: The manual is a local/repository artifact; publishing it to a public application route is a separate decision.
Current production technical hostname and Microsoft identities remain COEX-compatible. Product naming does not imply a new domain or app identity.

resolutions.title: Outlook iframe refused to connect
resolutions.status: Deployed; real Outlook web reads verified
resolutions.symptom: Worktello was listed in Outlook but its embedded screen was refused.
resolutions.cause: Exact Outlook web host was missing from frame-ancestors; the token verifier allowed Teams clients only.
resolutions.fix: Allow exact production Outlook web hosts/client; owner-approved preauthorization for the existing access_as_user scope.
resolutions.verification: 348 unit tests, local/server build and PR/main CI passed. Real Outlook web SSO, list, task detail and blank create form rendered; no production mutation sent.

resolutions.title: Search popup trapped by the header
resolutions.symptom: The popup position/layer could be affected by the header on intermediate screen widths.
resolutions.cause: A blurred/transformed ancestor contained the fixed overlay.
resolutions.fix: Render the popup in document.body and clamp it to the visible viewport; keep focus and stale-request handling.
resolutions.verification: Responsive synthetic/local QA and production permitted-result search documented.

resolutions.title: Subtask checkbox/count did not settle correctly
resolutions.symptom: Full-page checkbox state/count needed to follow server-confirmed toggling.
resolutions.cause: Uncontrolled checkbox state did not consistently track optimistic/reconciled state.
resolutions.fix: Use controlled completion state/count with existing action error rollback.
resolutions.verification: Synthetic check/uncheck/reload flow documented; no real production task mutated for demonstration.

resolutions.title: Tutorial link save showed Not allowed
resolutions.symptom: A valid tutorial link could be denied behind the production HTTPS proxy.
resolutions.cause: Browser public Origin was compared only with an internal listener origin.
resolutions.fix: Accept the exact configured public origin while keeping administrator and foreign-origin rejection.
resolutions.verification: Route regression, local/server build and public auth checks; signed-in save/playback not claimed.

resolutions.title: Microsoft login returned to localhost
resolutions.symptom: The callback could build a destination from the internal listener address.
resolutions.cause: Redirect origin did not consistently use the configured public application URL.
resolutions.fix: Use the configured canonical HTTPS origin for callback outcomes.
resolutions.verification: Redirect regressions and real production Microsoft sign-in on 25 October.

resolutions.title: Teams assignment email expectations
resolutions.symptom: Email was absent when assigning a Teams-created task to the creator.
resolutions.cause: Existing staff self-action suppression; another selected assignee received mail.
resolutions.fix: Retain intentional self-assignment suppression; reuse normal alerts for another assignee and tenant email switches.
resolutions.verification: Owner confirmed behavior; queue/service evidence retained. No real test mail sent by this manual.

resolutions.title: Patched Node runtime activation
resolutions.symptom: Production application processes still used the older Node runtime.
resolutions.cause: Updating requirements alone does not replace the executable of an already running process.
resolutions.fix: Install verified Node 22.23.4 side by side and activate explicit interpreters for web and one-at-a-time workers.
resolutions.verification: Actual parent/descendant executables under five PM2 entries verified. Host-global Node/PM2 daemon replacement was not claimed.
